[Supplementary Test Record-11]
"Failed the Originium Arts theory test, failed the Originium Arts practical test as well, and the only thing that reached Standard was your Assimilation... How many make-up tests does this make now? Maybe we should just...?"
"Aaaah! Th-then what if I try again with Grandma's pocket watch?"
"Hmm... That pocket watch really is a remarkable Arts Unit, but... ahem, if you can't learn it, no tool—however remarkable—is going to help."
(The sound of someone collapsing to the floor in despair)
"Aw, don't take it so hard. I felt exactly the same when I was studying math and physics. Some things you just can't learn... and that's that."

sections.title: Profile
sections.text: Thumpy, from Great Geyser Town in Rim Billiton, came to Rhodes Island for Oripathy treatment. On the recommendation of Operator Angelina, and in accordance with her own wishes, she joined the Field Operations Department as a Defender Operator to assist Rhodes Island.

sections.title: Clinical Analysis
sections.text:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 3%
A small amount of Originium crystals is distributed around Operator Thumpy's wrists.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.17u/L
Operator Thumpy's condition has been kept well under control and is currently relatively stable.

Upon learning that height measurements do not count ear length, Thumpy grew even fonder of the short ears she shares with her grandmother. But after being caught hiding a pair of height-boosting insoles, Thumpy looked more miserable than if she had bitten into a damp, stale carrot stick.

sections.title: Archive File 1
sections.text:
"(Extremely quietly) Yellow radish, green radish, pink radish, red radish."
"All right, Thumpy, what was the last line he just said?"
"Hehe, I heard it! It was 'pink radish, red radish'!"

On the day of her onboarding physical, Thumpy already displayed astonishing hearing. Whether it was pinpointing sounds by ear, the frequency range test, or even identifying exactly which line an Operator was murmuring in the corner of another room from "Radishes," Rim Billiton's hardest tongue twister, Thumpy performed superbly. More and more people came to watch the hearing test. Closure joined the fun with an instrument in hand and asked Thumpy to listen for where the fault was; when Thumpy pinpointed the problem on the spot, Closure eagerly invited her to join the Engineering Department as a maintenance engineer. A Medic Operator who had been busy next door brought over an assortment of hearing aids to see whether she could tell them apart; Vigna came with her guitar so Thumpy could hear the difference in tone between the strings; and Lee, out for a stroll, produced a dice cup to see whether she could hear what numbers had been rolled...
The little commotion finally ended when everyone—no keen hearing required—could hear Thumpy's stomach growling. They all pulled out their meal cards to buy her a meal as thanks, and while they ate together they went on discussing where Thumpy's career might take her. At that point a few Archosaurians grew curious: "Do Rim Billitonians have any sort of long-ear versus short-ear factional feud?"
Thumpy's first response was "Absolutely not," but after a moment's thought she revised it to "There might be, but I've never paid attention." Then she added proudly, "Because my ears look exactly like Grandma's!"

sections.title: Archive File 2
sections.text:
The thirteenth Originium Arts Assimilation test once again ended with a grade of "Standard." Thumpy found that nothing could change the reality of her utter lack of talent for Originium Arts—not taking the field with her grandmother's Arts Unit pocket watch, not memorizing Arts theory back to front, not begging Angelina for special training, not even copying Timeslot by kneeling on the floor before the test and pleading with her Arts Unit to work: "Why didn't I inherit Grandma's talent for Originium Arts?!"
Whether Originium Arts Assimilation is hereditary remains medically unsettled, and the notion that a grandmother passes certain traits on to her granddaughter has no theoretical grounding either. Even so, Thumpy has always believed her grandmother handed a great deal down to her, and those signature short ears and pale pink hair are her strongest evidence.
On the strength of this "theory of inheritance," Thumpy chalks all sorts of feats up to the strength and wisdom she inherited from her grandmother, or to following in her grandmother's footsteps: she too pulled a trapped person out from underground all by herself, she too crossed the length of Rim Billiton, and she too reached the fabled Southern Reaches said to hold the most beautiful scenery of all...
Thumpy herself knows, of course, that what she accomplished has nothing to do with heredity. What is more, there is a long distance between "wanting to do something" and "actually having done it"—and Thumpy has already crossed that distance, growing step by step into a stronger version of herself.

Thumpy suddenly asked one of our Medic Operators just now whether she might have inherited her grandmother's height as well, and whether she could still grow a little taller. Well... Grandma Inara is the sort of Cautus exceptionally gifted in both height and build, and given Thumpy's current age, she is unlikely to ever grow as tall and imposing as her grandmother!

No way, no way, no way! I can still grow taller!
—Thumpy

sections.title: Archive File 3
sections.text:
Living in a country with a vast population, Rim Billitonians are used to giving everyone around them a distinctive nickname, so that they can quickly tell which of the many people sharing a name is meant. Thumpy has quite a few nicknames of her own.
As a child she was called "Little Doll," because she was small in stature, small in the ears, small in everything. Whenever she wanted to play with the others, they would laugh and say, "Little Doll's too little, she can't do this," and leave her out. Thumpy was not happy about it, because she wanted to play too and believed she could manage it, so she never liked that nickname.
Later Thumpy picked up a few more nicknames. "Brainy," because she could remember the name of nearly everyone in town; and "Switchboard," simply because she worked as the town's switchboard operator... Back then she could not really say she disliked them, but she grew ever more envious of her grandmother's nickname: "Inara the Pathfinder"—how commanding, how impressive! "If only I had a nickname like that..." Thumpy says she used to imagine it from time to time.
That wish came true before long.
On the way back from the Southern Reaches to Great Geyser Town, Thumpy was delighted to find that at nearly every stop she passed through there were still people who remembered her—and had even given her new nicknames:
"Loudmouth"—because she hollered the whole way while she and Jacinta went tearing off in a car to save a friend; "Big Heart"—given by the people of Artichoke Village in thanks for speaking up for Amelia, which was what finally got their communications tower repaired; "Short-Ears Tani"—the miners of Sun Valley Industries, grateful to her for rescuing their repairman, borrowed the prefix from her grandmother's nickname; "Little Hero"—what Thumpy's parents and her dozens of relatives call her now, because their brave little Thumpy did the thing she had said she wanted to do before setting out and fulfilled her dream; and "Wayfinder"—the Thumpy of today has left Rim Billiton behind and travels the vast land of Terra with our field squad, searching out places where more of the Infected can live.

Hehe, I forgot to say where the name "Thumpy" comes from! It's because I'm always stomping around thump-thump-thump, so Grandma gave me this pet name that means "thump-thump stomping." My family calls me that when they want to cheer me up, too, so I picked it for my codename!
—Thumpy

sections.title: Archive File 4
sections.text:
Recently an Operator who had come out at night looking for snacks filed a terrified report claiming she had witnessed a paranormal incident: she had seen a backpack moving through an empty corridor all on its own. A number of others soon came forward saying they had had the same experience—but after checking the security footage, everyone realized it was simply Thumpy running down the corridor on an emergency deployment.
True enough, that enormous backpack is the first impression many Operators have of Thumpy. But anyone who has watched her in the training room—getting back up no matter how many times she falls or how many times her own backpack knocks her flat, drilling over and over how to fight in concert with it—or who has been on a field mission with her and seen that tiny figure sling the pack onto her back and get straight to work, comes away thinking less about the enormous backpack and more about Thumpy herself: small in stature, yet always brimming with drive and courage.
As for where that courage comes from, Thumpy herself cannot explain it. In fact she has always been the most timid one in her family—take the thirty-odd failed attempts at running away from home that her parents love to bring up, each of them ending with her frightened back the moment she stepped outside the town.
Perhaps it was because there were so many children in the house, and the endless problems they generated every day kept everyone too busy: nobody noticed the tenacity behind Thumpy's thirty-odd attempts, and nobody imagined she would try a fortieth time, or a fiftieth—until she really did walk out of the town and reach the Southern Reaches. It was only after Thumpy came back that they even learned she could drive. She knew her family never took her dream of going out to explore very seriously, but she carried a determination to leave all the same, so she simply learned in secret: on the first day the roar of the engine startled a scream out of her; on the second, a speed she failed to control frightened her so badly that her tears flew onto the window; on the third, she lost track of when the geysers would erupt and the water nearly flipped the car, leaving her too scared to get behind the wheel for three days... And yet, having never actually left her town or driven on anything like a proper road, Thumpy honed her driving bit by bit until she could take turns at the wheel with Angelina on Highway Zero without anyone spotting her as a novice and without a single incident.
So the source of that courage may be the unshakable determination Thumpy brings to whatever she sets out to do, or it may be that she has already failed countless times where no one was watching—and so she is not afraid of failing again, because she knows she will always try once more, right up until the day she succeeds.
Perhaps the protagonist of the next legend will be Thumpy herself—
That is one of the most fervent hopes of this writer, whose ears have long since grown calluses from all the "Grandma stories."

sections.title: Promotion Record
sections.text:
Thumpy recently announced out of the blue that she wanted to make a trip to a certain uninhabited region of Rim Billiton.
There is no habitable land there worth surveying, nor any spectacular scenery. The only thing special about it may be that, with not a soul for a hundred miles in any direction, the nights there are utterly, absolutely dark.
Once her bags were packed, Thumpy set out. After several days of trekking she finally reached the place, and just as she finished pitching her tent, night fell at last.
The night swallowed the whole expanse like a rising tide; the only things glimmering there were Thumpy's headlamp on the ground and the scattered stars in the sky. Thumpy took out her telescope and camera, aimed the lenses at the faintly glowing starry sky, and began to search.
She swept past the Milky Way, past the morning star, past countless beautiful seas of stars, until she found that familiar glow: the two stars, one pink and one gold, keeping each other company side by side, appeared before her at last with perfect clarity.
Thumpy pressed the shutter and captured this beautiful night sky.
